chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: عَلِيٌّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، وَمُحَحَّمَدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعًا، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَصَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى جَمِيعًا، عَنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, all together, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ أَصَابَا صَيْدًا وَهُمَا مُحْرِمَانِ الْجَزَاءُ بَيْنَهُمَا أَوْ عَلَى كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا جَزَاءٌ؟ فَقَالَ: بَلْ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُجْزِيَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا الصَّيْدَ، قُلْتُ: إِنَّ بَعْضَ أَصْحَابِنَا سَأَلَنِي عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: إِذَا أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَ هَذَا فَلَمْ تَدْرُوا فَعَلَيْكُم بِالِاحْتِيَاطِ حَتَّى تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ فَتَعْلَمُوا

translations.en: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about two men who killed game while they were in Ihram – is the atonement shared between them or is it on each one of them individually? He said: Rather, it is incumbent upon both that each one of them atones for the game. I said: One of our companions asked me about that but I did not know what was incumbent upon him, so he said: If you encounter the like of this and do not know, then upon you is acting by precaution until you ask about it and know.

en.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that in cases of joint action by two individuals in Ihram, the atonement (jaza') is cumulative rather than shared, establishing individual liability for each participant. This ruling is coupled with the broader jurisprudential principle of *al-ihitiyat* (precaution), which mandates seeking definitive knowledge when faced with legal uncertainty to ensure religious compliance. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for understanding the distinction between shared obligations and individual duties in ritual law.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on atonement when two people in Ihram kill game together, and what is the principle of precaution?

key_terms.مُحْرِمَانِ: Two men in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الِاحْتِيَاط: Precaution (acting cautiously in matters of religious law when uncertain)
